note: Conservative production heuristics, not guarantees. Decoration aliases and rules are both checked in order; the first match wins. Every outcome still needs the producer's confirmation.

rules.notes: Water-based inks need an absorbent fibre; coated or DWR-finished nylon repels them and the print will not bond or survive washing.
rules.confirm: Ask the producer which bonding method they use for this shell fabric.

rules.notes: High curing temperatures can glaze, scorch, or shrink heat-sensitive synthetics and stretch fibres.
rules.confirm: Ask the producer for their press temperature limit on this fabric.

rules.notes: Sublimation dye only bonds with polyester and shows only on light grounds; it fades or fails on cotton.
rules.confirm: Confirm the fibre content with the producer before choosing sublimation.

rules.notes: Sublimation is a transparent dye; it cannot print light colours onto a dark garment.
rules.confirm: Confirm the base colour and method with the producer.

rules.notes: Plastisol on coated nylon needs a nylon bonding additive and a test print; adhesion varies by coating.
rules.confirm: Ask the producer for a wash-tested sample on the exact shell fabric.

rules.notes: Use a low-temperature transfer rated for the fibre; standard transfers can scorch synthetics.
rules.confirm: Ask the producer which transfer film and temperature they will use.

rules.notes: Limited spot-colour screen printing suits cotton and cotton blends. Each colour needs its own screen; dark garments need a white underbase for light inks.
rules.confirm: Confirm the producer's colour-count limit and whether an underbase is required.

rules.notes: More than six spot colours usually needs simulated process separations or a different method.
rules.confirm: Ask the producer how many screens their press supports and review a strike-off.

rules.notes: DTG suits detailed raster artwork on untreated cotton; dark garments need pretreatment and colours print less saturated than screen print.
rules.confirm: Ask the producer for a sample print on the chosen garment colour.

rules.notes: Full-colour sublimation suits white or light polyester; seams and folds can leave unprinted creases on finished garments.
rules.confirm: Confirm with the producer whether they print cut panels or finished garments.

rules.notes: Embroidery suits stable wovens and heavy knits. Keep text at least about 5 mm tall and satin columns at least about 1 mm wide.
rules.confirm: Send the artwork to the producer's digitiser and approve a sew-out.

rules.notes: Light or stretchy knits pucker under dense stitching; use a stabiliser and lighter fill, or a patch.
rules.confirm: Ask the producer for a sew-out on the exact fabric.
